standard: Current local canonical docs/teaching-standard-and-practice.md v1.12 (14 October 2026), fixed editorial-reference/m101-opening-chapter-v0.4.html; both inspected, not inferred from the older project header.
curriculum: Approved Stage 1 outcomes O1/O5/O6, M101 B02/U04–U07 and complete Block 2 lesson blueprint; 72 block hours remain unchanged; assessment adds its already allocated six hours.

comparisons.source: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, section 2.3, Limit Laws; Examples 2.19–2.22 and their working
comparisons.inspected: Actual explanatory text, algebraic limit examples and piecewise one-sided example.
comparisons.relevance: Distinguishing nearby equality, missing values, domains and one-sided evidence.
comparisons.difference: TMA requires an independently justified extension and a first-principles derivative; source includes scaffolded worked explanations. No direct supplied private OU introductory-calculus match was available.

comparisons.source: Released M101 U05 L05 section 5.25, Example 5.21 and Activity 5.25; U05 L01 section 5.5
comparisons.inspected: Actual one-sided quotient working, continuity condition and counterexamples.
comparisons.relevance: All-pair classification before differentiability; a continuous counterexample.
comparisons.difference: TMA adds explicit family classification and a learner-chosen counterexample; no worked feedback or graph supplies the answer. Private OU material inspected contains no matched join exercise.

comparisons.source: Private OU MST224 Unit 1, printed pages 42–46, Exercises 27, 29–32, worked Examples 3–4 and implicit-ellipse exposition; page 45 also rendered and visually inspected
comparisons.relevance: Rule combinations, second derivatives and implicit chain/product reasoning.
comparisons.difference: OU text revises prior calculus; M101 is first teaching. TMA uses an exponential of a trigonometric function, not the source's damped-oscillation product, and combines a mixed implicit relation with a second derivative. No proprietary wording or worked material is republished.

comparisons.source: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1 section 3.8, implicit differentiation exposition and Examples 3.69 and 3.73
comparisons.relevance: Dependent-variable chain factors and tangent conditions.
comparisons.difference: TMA also assesses a second differentiation; actual released M101 section 5.24, Example 5.20 and Activity 5.24 supply that prerequisite.

comparisons.source: Private OU MST224 Unit 1, printed pages 46–50, investigating-functions exposition, Exercise 33, worked Example 5 and Exercise 34
comparisons.relevance: Domain-aware stationary candidates, sign changes, concavity and global/end-point reasoning.
comparisons.difference: TMA consolidates these ideas in one closed-domain polynomial rather than the source's exponential and rational cases; no sketch or graphing tool is mandatory. Endpoints and a deliberately excluded stationary candidate require domain selection.

comparisons.source: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1 section 4.4, Rolle's theorem statement and three-case proof; released M101 section 6.15, Example 6.14 and Activity 6.15
comparisons.relevance: Closed-interval continuity, interior differentiability, and an interior point with the average slope.
comparisons.difference: TMA asks for application and all admissible inputs, not reproduction of a proof. No matched private OU passage inspected for this theorem.

comparisons.source: Released M101 section 6.11, Example 6.10 and Activity 6.11; OpenStax Calculus Volume 1 section 4.1, Example 4.1 with solution
comparisons.relevance: Differentiate before evaluating an instant, common time variable, units and signed rates.
comparisons.difference: TMA's geometry was drafted before the public-source comparison; it requires a second related surface-area rate and only instantaneous given data. Sensor time rate transfers the same reasoning. No matched private OU rates question was located among inspected pages.

comparisons.source: Released M101 section 7.1, Example 7.1 and Activity 7.1; OpenStax Calculus Volume 1 section 4.2, Linear Approximation of a Function at a Point, reciprocal example and tangent formula
comparisons.relevance: Value plus predicted change; compare a local model with exact values.
comparisons.difference: Original sensor polynomial permits a rigorous elementary tolerance interval without Taylor theory, experimental data or a thermometry prerequisite. Source's differentials and percentage-error material are not assumed.

comparisons.source: Released M101 U07 L03 section 7.14, actual code, Activity 7.14 and discussion; U05 section 5.5; Fundamentals of Numerical Computation section 5.5, convergence table, section 5.5.2 stability discussion and Example 5.5.4
comparisons.relevance: Hand/code comparison, floating-point input guards, non-monotone refinement, output-scale effects and a reproducible run.
comparisons.difference: FNC assumes more numerical-analysis/Taylor background. TMA uses only taught finite differences, a rational hand benchmark and one-sided reasoning at a corner; no order proof, optimal-step formula or plotting. Compared with the 120-minute supported Unit 7 activity, this is a 90-minute independent retrieval/transfer task with seven prescribed steps, simple tables and a short report.

actualAdjoiningPassagesRead: U07 L03 section 7.14 / Activity 7.14 and code

gaps: Supplied MST124 introductory-calculus chapter is unavailable. MST224 is a revision comparator, not a first-teaching match. No claim is made to private OU comparison for topics absent from the inspected pages, external human moderation or a learner timing trial.
originality: Original assessment wording, integrated contexts, expressions and mark design. Standard mathematical forms are necessarily shared. No private source pages, source solutions or marking guide are part of the public package.
